title: Learning Peer Influence Probabilities with Linear Contextual Bandits

problem.claim: The work studies how to learn peer influence probabilities under contextual variation in networked recommendations.

gap.claim: Static data can capture correlations but not influence relationships, while existing online approaches either waste resources through random exploration or optimize rewards rather than estimation accuracy.

contributions.claim: Characterizes all achievable rate pairs for the trade-off between regret minimization and estimation error.
Proposes an uncertainty-guided exploration algorithm that can attain any rate pair within the regret–estimation-error trade-off by tuning a parameter.
Evaluates the method on semi-synthetic network datasets against static methods and contextual bandits that ignore the trade-off.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on semi-synthetic network datasets show advantages of the proposed method over static methods and contextual bandits that ignore the trade-off.

narrative_sequence.summary: Peer recommendations are common, and whether they are acted upon depends on multiple contextual factors.
Peer influence probabilities vary substantially, and estimating them supports information-diffusion understanding and viral-marketing effectiveness.
Static data cannot identify influence relationships, while existing online approaches have exploration or reward-optimization limitations.
The paper formulates the problem as a contextual linear bandit and develops a trade-off characterization with uncertainty-guided exploration.
Semi-synthetic network experiments report advantages over specified comparison methods.

source_observation.claim: Learning influence probabilities involves a trade-off between regret minimization and estimation error.

interpretation.claim: When the goal includes accurate estimation rather than reward alone, exploration should account explicitly for both objectives.

application.claim: Use tunable uncertainty-guided exploration when an online decision problem requires balancing performance and parameter estimation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this trade-off or algorithm generalizes beyond the stated peer-influence setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal model, assumptions, or rate definitions.
The abstract does not report dataset details, quantitative results, or statistical uncertainty.
The abstract does not describe the algorithm's computational complexity or implementation details.
